content_plan.quick-dinner: A complete weeknight dinner built around one hero ingredient that comes together fast. Slide 1: hero shot of the finished dish plated beautifully — rich colour, glossy sauce, clean surface, pure food photography with absolutely no text, numbers, or labels on the image. Slide 2: flat-lay of the raw ingredients loosely arranged by colour — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3-4: a two-beat visual sequence showing one key technique moment (e.g. a vigorous sear, sauce reducing in the pan) followed by the finished, plated result — no text overlays of any kind. Final slide: tight close-up of texture and colour detail that makes the dish feel craveable and achievable. ALL ingredient quantities, timing, steps, swaps, and any written information belong in the caption only.
content_plan.marinade: One complete marinade built around a single protein or seasonal occasion. Slide 1: hero shot of the marinated, deeply coloured, glistening protein on a clean dark or neutral surface — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, or labels anywhere on the image. Slide 2: aesthetic flat-lay of raw marinade ingredients grouped loosely by colour and texture — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3-4: visual process contrast — protein submerging into the marinade, then the vivid colour and sheen transformation after marinating — no overlaid text or graphics of any kind. Final slide: finished plated dish in warm directional light, garnished but not cluttered. ALL ratios, quantities, timing, substitution tips, and step information belong in the caption exclusively.
content_plan.technique: One foundational cooking technique relevant to home cooks — e.g. how to build a fond, reverse-sear, bloom spices, or emulsify a pan sauce. Slide 1: hero shot of the dramatic visual payoff of the technique (e.g. a perfectly seared crust, a glossy emulsified sauce) — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, labels, or graphics anywhere on the image. Slide 2: flat-lay or close-up of the key tools or ingredients that make the technique work — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3-4: two-beat before/after visual sequence showing the technique mid-action and the finished result — no text overlays of any kind. Final slide: close-up detail of the texture, colour, or finish that makes the result unmistakably worth the technique. ALL explanations, ratios, timing, troubleshooting tips, and step-by-step instructions belong in the caption exclusively.

caption_strategy: Every caption must earn a save before it earns a follow. Open with a single punchy hook line that names the specific dish or technique and a concrete benefit (e.g. 'This 20-minute garlic-butter chicken will wreck your takeaway habit'). Follow immediately with the full recipe or technique steps — quantities, timing, substitutions — written in plain numbered or bulleted lines so the caption is genuinely useful as a standalone reference. Close with one low-friction CTA focused on saving ('Save this before tonight's shop') rather than following. Use natural, search-friendly language throughout: name the protein, the technique, the cuisine style, and the occasion in the first three lines, because Instagram indexes captions for keyword search. Avoid generic closers like 'Let me know in the comments' — they do not drive the sends or saves that grow a young account.
hashtag_strategy: Use exactly 3-5 hashtags per post, placed at the end of the caption after a line break. Prioritise mid-size, topically specific tags (roughly 50k-500k posts) over massive generic ones: for example #weeknightdinner, #marinaderecipe, #cookingtechnique, #easychickenrecipe, #homecooking. Avoid tags above 5M posts — they bury new accounts instantly. Rotate the set slightly each post to gather data on which tags correlate with higher reach. Do not use hashtags as the primary growth lever; keyword-rich caption text and saves/sends are the real signals at this stage.
learnings: All 22 posts show zero sends, saves, and follows — reach is real but engagement is not converting at all. This is the critical problem: the account is being seen (reach 1.0-2.0) but not saved or shared. Priority shift: make every caption a genuinely useful, complete reference (full recipe with quantities, timing, substitutions) so viewers have a concrete reason to save. Retire the 'sauce' theme (6 posts, lowest reach at 1.5, zero engagement) — reallocate its slots to quick-dinner, which has the highest reach and fewest posts. Drop w0-19 (reach 1.3, worst slot) and w6-10 (reach 1.0). Hold cadence at 4/week until saves or sends register.
